The latest commit raised the script's wait to 90s without raising the stage timeout, so Jenkins interrupted the script at 59-60s and aborted the build.

[10:55:12] Cancelling nested steps due to timeout

diagnosis.suggested_fix: Make the Jenkins stage timeout consistent with the smoke test's wait. Set the Smoke Test stage timeout in the Jenkinsfile to comfortably exceed the script's 90s wait (e.g. 3 minutes), ideally by sharing one value so they cannot drift apart. Also confirm why the service needs up to 90s to become healthy.
assumptions: The 1 minute timeout is defined in the Jenkinsfile Smoke Test stage; the Jenkinsfile contents are not shown.
The 90s wait in scripts/smoke_test.py is the value changed by the latest commit, inferred from the commit message and log output.
The service would become healthy within 90s; the log does not show whether it ever would.
